researcher: Codex parallel release158-haripunjaya-shared research, integrated by Codex

sources.title: Human History Map civilization index
sources.note: Exact Haripunjaya 1000 to 1100 and Harapunchai 1200 to 1279 generated records, spellings, circa flags, and map intervals.

sources.title: Human History Map imported summaries
sources.note: Byte-identical imported summaries connect both ids to one Lamphun-centered Mon kingdom but are not used as independent historical authority.

sources.title: Human History Map research coverage registry
sources.note: Exact missing-card status, one snapshot per target, and unreviewed identity, chronology, and border fields.

sources.title: Human History Map 900 borders
sources.note: Pre-start seam control showing Lamphun-area probes assigned to the imported Khmer Empire feature.

sources.title: Human History Map 1000 borders
sources.note: Sole Haripunjaya feature, decoded geometry, point membership, direct shared arcs, and exact geometry hashes.

sources.title: Human History Map 1100 borders
sources.note: Gap-start seam assigning the Lamphun core to an implausibly broad Kingdom of Sukhotai feature.

sources.title: Human History Map 1200 borders
sources.note: Sole Harapunchai feature, decoded geometry, point membership, shared arcs, and later expanded polygon.

sources.title: Human History Map 1279 borders
sources.note: Endpoint seam assigning Lamphun and most tested places to Sukhothai before Mangrai conquered Hariphunchai.

sources.title: Human History Map 1300 borders
sources.note: Post-end control showing the atlas assignments persist through 1300 despite the separate 1292 Lan Na conquest chronology.

sources.title: Ancient Haripunjaya based on archaeological evidence
sources.note: Silpakorn University doctoral study dividing habitation into eighth to ninth, tenth to eleventh, and twelfth to fourteenth-century stages, with Dvaravati, Pyu-Pagan, Khmer, and local elements.

sources.title: Conservation and management of historic settlements in northern Thailand
sources.note: University of York heritage thesis treating Hariphunchai as the earliest historically attested northern city-state and distinguishing archaeological evidence, later traditions, and later Lan Na development.

sources.title: Chiang Mai between Empire and Modern Thailand: The City Founded
sources.note: Open-access scholarly chapter on Hariphunchai urban hierarchy, satellite communities, mixed local and Mon formation, and Mangrai capture in 1292.

sources.title: Dvaravati Art in Haripunjaya
sources.note: Silpakorn University study of Wat Ku Kut and octagonal stupa phases, identifying Dvaravati, Lopburi, Pagan, and distinctive local features.

sources.title: Ceramic Wares of the Haripunjaya Area
sources.note: Journal of the Siam Society archaeological study of dated pottery, spindle whorls, pellets, votive plaques, regional links, and production continuing after political takeover.

sources.title: Notes on Mon Epigraphy II
sources.note: Christian Bauer edition of twelfth to thirteenth-century Old Mon inscriptions on Saraphi votive tablets, with facsimiles, Roman transliteration, and translation of the honorific.

sources.title: Svavadhisiddhi Inscription 1, Wat Don Kaew
sources.note: Official Thai inscription database record for a seventeenth Buddhist-century Old Mon and Pali royal donation mentioning monasteries, scripture, stupas, relatives, consorts, a son, land, and dependents.

sources.title: Svavadhisiddhi Inscription 1 transcription and translation
sources.note: Official scholarly text edition with Pali benediction, construction sequence, land, and counted male and female temple dependents and kitchen workers.

sources.title: Svavadhisiddhi Inscription 2, Wat Ku Kut
sources.note: Official Old Mon and Pali inscription record for earthquake repair, stupas, royal donations, a monastery well, temple dependents, and the king mother participation.

sources.title: Wat Saen Khao Ho Inscription
sources.note: Official Old Mon inscription record for Buddha images, Bodhi and coconut trees, a parasol, manuscript storage, a wall, and a donated pair of cattle.

sources.title: Wiang Mano Inscription
sources.note: Official database record for an Old Mon and Old Burmese inscription reused on a slate grinding stone, with debated eleventh or twelfth-century dating.

sources.title: Old Mon Votive Tablet Inscription 2
sources.note: Official record of a single Old Mon line on a twelfth to thirteenth-century terracotta tablet from Saraphi naming Pindola-Bharadvaja.

sources.title: Old Mon Votive Tablet Inscription 3
sources.note: Official record of a single Old Mon line on a twelfth to thirteenth-century terracotta tablet from Saraphi naming Bhaddiya and discussing inexpensive clay votives cautiously.

sources.title: Wat Mahawan Inscription edition
sources.note: Official edition of a damaged Old Mon inscription recording donations, metal values, an artisan, sacred buildings, images, and temple dependents, with uncertain readings retained.

sources.title: Natural degradation of earthworks, trenches, walls and moats: northern Thailand
sources.note: Field archaeology study of Lamphun and nearby settlements, conch or rectangular plans, walls, moats, reservoirs, floodplain location, and dating limits.

sources.title: Southeast Asian ceramics chronology: Haripunjaya
sources.note: Smithsonian regional chronology giving Lamphun as capital and a differing 1281 absorption date, useful for presenting chronological disagreement after 1279.

sources.title: Lanna Legal History: From Customary Laws to Modern Law
sources.note: Peer-reviewed Thai Legal Studies article distinguishing Hariphunchai annexation in 1292 from Lan Na and Chiang Mai foundation in 1296; used only for the ending synthesis.

sources.title: Review of A Brief History of Lan Na
sources.note: Peer-reviewed book review explicitly flags the Hariphunchai conquest as 1281 or 1292 and distinguishes the later Lan Na political and cultural formation.

sources.title: Votive tablet depicting eighteen Buddhas
sources.note: Smithsonian museum object record for a late thirteenth-century terracotta tablet from Lamphun, with dimensions and material.

sources.title: San-Ku archaeological site on Doi Pui
sources.note: Chiang Mai University arts journal excavation report on a brick vihara and stupa with eleventh to twelfth-century Hariphunchai-style votive tablets in a Lawa-associated sacred landscape.

sources.title: Palaeochannels of the Ping River and archaeological settlements
sources.note: Geomorphological study comparing old Ping channels with Lamphun and later settlements, useful for landscape history and chronological restraint.

sources.title: Hariphunchai National Museum: About the collection
sources.note: Fine Arts Department museum account of its inscription collection, including eight Old Mon inscriptions from Lamphun and the modern history of their study.

sources.title: Phra Perm votive tablet
sources.note: Fine Arts Department museum object record dating a terracotta votive tablet to the eleventh or twelfth century and noting Pagan, Pala, and Gupta-related visual influence.

sources.title: Inscriptions in Thailand, volume 2
sources.note: National Library of Thailand official inscription edition used to cross-check Old Mon corpus identity, chronology, and the limits of machine-readable script.
